messages:
From: John Park <j.park@acmehealth.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: security-ops@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Private deployment egress — allowlist and proxy questions

Hi Irene / Laura,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. We're in the middle of our network security review and need a couple of concrete confirmations to close the outbound / allowlist section: 

- Do you publish a stable set of IPv4/IPv6 addresses for outbound control-plane traffic for a VPC/private deployment, or is outbound routed through customer-managed NAT only?
- If Redwood provides an egress gateway, can it be pinned to a static IP for contractual purposes?
- Do you support mutual-TLS to an outbound proxy (we use an internal proxy that must authenticate with client certs)?

Attached is the portion of our questionnaire that references outbound and firewall requirements (redacted). Can you confirm what evidence you can provide for our auditors (e.g., egress IP list, test connectivity scripts, or a signed statement)?

Goal: we need a short acceptance bundle by EOW Friday so procurement can finish the PO.

Regards,
John Park
Head of IT Security — Acme Health
(attachment: acme_s2_questionnaire.pdf)
From: irene.choi@redwood.com
To: John Park <j.park@acmehealth.com>, security-ops@acmehealth.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 12:34:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment egress — allowlist and proxy questions

John — thanks for the clear list. Summary answers up front: we can provide a contractual static egress IP when using Redwood-managed egress gateway (Dedicated or Private managed gateway), and we can support mTLS to a customer proxy with a short ops integration; we also provide an evidence bundle for audits.

Details / asks:
- Egress options: we offer three patterns: customer-NAT-only (customer owns IPs), redwood-managed static egress (we allocate an IP that we guarantee in the contract), or ephemeral egress (for burst scenarios — not suitable for allowlisting). Please confirm which model you prefer.
- If you opt for redwood-managed static egress, we need a lead time of 10 business days to allocate and update routing during onboarding.
- For mTLS to a customer proxy: we will need the CA chain and naming expectations; our ops team will schedule a handshake window.
- Evidence pack: we can provide a signed egress-address attestation, a connectivity test script (curl + expected SNI), and a capture of firewall flows from our staging gateway.

I'm attaching a draft allowlist matrix I put together — it maps control plane endpoints, telemetry endpoints, and optional managed-egress IPs (redwood-egress-matrix.csv). Please review and flag any missing FQDNs or internal IPs.

Proposed next steps:
1) You confirm preferred egress model by Thu 07/02
2) We send final contract clause and IP list by Fri 07/03
3) Ops runs mTLS handshake test the week of 07/06 if needed

cheers,
Irene Choi
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood-egress-matrix.csv)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment egress — allowlist and proxy questions

Looping in some contract wording we should offer Acme. Laura — suggesting we include a short SLA bullet that the provided static IPs will not change without 30 days' notice (except in documented emergency). Draft clause below — feel free to edit before sending to John: 

-- draft egress clause START --
Redwood will provide Customer with a set of static IPv4 addresses for outbound traffic originating from Redwood-managed egress gateways associated with the Customer's Private Deployment. Redwood warrants that these IP addresses will remain assigned to the Customer's deployment for the duration of the Term, except where emergency reallocation is necessary for security or operational reasons; in such cases Redwood will provide as much notice as practicable and no less than 30 calendar days where feasible.
-- draft egress clause END --

Operational notes: if Acme requires mTLS to their proxy we will need the certs and a sandbox proxy endpoint to complete a handshake. Also adding a small ops checklist to the shared Drive: onboarding-routing.txt and sample curl test.

Ben Carter
Senior Product Security, Redwood Inference
(attachment: draft-egress-clause.docx)
From: John Park <j.park@acmehealth.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, security-ops@acmehealth.com
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2026 22:03:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment egress — allowlist and proxy questions

Irene / Ben / Laura — this is helpful, thanks. Acme confirms we want the Redwood-managed static egress option and we can provide the CA chain and a sandbox proxy for the handshake. Procurement wants the IP list and the contract clause as the final artifacts to sign off.

Action items we will take:
- Send CA chain and sandbox proxy details to Irene by Mon 07/05
- Proc will review the draft egress clause; we may propose a 60-day notice window instead of 30 — we'll share redlines by Tue 07/06

Request for Redwood: please attach the signed egress attestation PDF and the final CSV with the IPs (not a placeholder) when you send the redlines back. If you can get those to us by EOD Wed 07/08 that keeps procurement on schedule.

Thanks — looking forward to finishing this out.
John
Head of IT Security — Acme Health
